title: Internal Unit Economics Dashboard v1 — scope + rollout epic
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
## Summary
Build and roll out an internal-only “Unit Economics” dashboard in the Redwood Console that provides a finance-aligned, trusted definition of **blended $/1M output tokens**, with drilldowns by **model (incl. version/quant profile)**, **region**, and **customer tier**.

This epic is the scope + delivery wrapper across Product/Console/Telemetry/Finance/SRE.

## Why this matters
We currently have partial cost reporting (infra spend) and partial metering (tokens), but no single place that:
- reconciles in a finance-friendly way
- is drilldownable by the dimensions teams actually use to make decisions
- is dependable enough for exec/KPI reporting

Primary outcomes:
- Enable cost optimization automation work by quantifying impact + catching regressions.
- Reduce time-to-diagnosis for “why did $/token move?” questions.
- Provide a repeatable reconciliation loop with Finance (rate card + allocation policy versioning).

## v1 Scope (what we will ship)
### 1) Canonical metric + definitions (finance-aligned)
- A single definition for **blended $/1M output tokens** including:
  - cost inputs (GPU rate card + allocation approach)
  - token attribution rules (output tokens are the denominator; consistent across streaming/non-streaming)
  - inclusion/exclusion rules (internal traffic, tests, retries, etc.)
  - dimension definitions + normalization (model/version/quant, region, customer tier)
- Versioning expectations (rate card updates + attribution model changes are tracked and auditable)

### 2) Data model + warehouse outputs
- Hourly aggregation job producing tables/views that support:
  - time series trends
  - breakdown tables (top-N models/regions/tiers)
  - drilldown queries with filters (time range, model, region, tier)
- Backfill for 2025 Q1 coverage to enable Finance QTD reporting

### 3) Console backend APIs
- Internal endpoints for:
  - time series (group_by dimension, filters)
  - breakdown tables (top-N + pagination)
  - drilldown details for a selected row (e.g., model → model version/quant profile)
- Caching/rate limiting tuned for internal usage, with a “live” view and a “finance” view option if needed for freshness vs stability

### 4) Console UI (internal-only)
- Internal Unit Economics page with:
  - filter bar: time range, model, region, customer tier
  - blended $/1M output tokens time series
  - top-N tables (by model/region/tier) with drilldown navigation
  - empty/error states per UX spec
  - formatting/rounding guidelines to avoid misinterpretation

### 5) Operational readiness
- Data quality checks (completeness, missing dimensions, sudden drops/drift)
- SLOs + alert routing + runbook links
- RBAC + feature flag, internal-only allowlist at launch, audit logs for access
- Reconciliation report vs billing totals (with known limitations documented)

## Explicit Non-goals (v1)
- Customer-facing cost dashboards or exposing unit economics externally
- Automated “do the optimization” actions (this project provides measurement + diagnostics)
- Per-customer drilldowns that risk exposing sensitive customer-identifiable information in the UI

## Milestones (proposed)
- Wk 1–2: Metric definition + dimension mapping sign-off (Finance + Eng) (PM-483)
- Wk 3–6: Telemetry + aggregation implementation; first warehouse views; initial API contract
- Wk 5–8: Console UI + backend endpoints; dogfood with Finance/Product/Eng
- Wk 8–10: Data quality hardening; SLO/alerts; runbooks; access controls
- Wk 10–12: Staged rollout + exec readout; backlog grooming for v1.1

## Acceptance criteria (definition of done)
1) **Metric trust / reconciliation**
- Finance (Laura/Rishi) signs off on methodology (rate card provenance, allocation policy, treatment of idle/shared overhead) and it is documented in the metric dictionary.
- Reconciliation report exists and is reviewed in at least 2 consecutive weekly closes with variance explained and within agreed tolerance.

2) **Token metering parity**
- Output token denominator is consistent across streaming and non-streaming paths.
- Regression tests exist for streaming output token counting and common edge cases (tool calls, truncation).

3) **Dimensions are usable and stable**
- Model identifiers are normalized such that grouping is consistent across gateway/runtime/analytics.
- Region normalization is implemented with canonical mapping + null/unknown handling.
- Customer tier mapping is implemented with an authoritative source, documented edge cases (resellers, pilots, credits), and backfill.
- Telemetry dimensions comply with cardinality standards (quant profile allowed-value constraints).

4) **Dashboard UX is actionable**
- Console page supports filters (time/model/region/tier) and drilldowns; top-N tables match UX spec.
- Cost metric is displayed in $/1M output tokens with consistent rounding and a visible note on known limitations.

5) **Operational readiness**
- Pipeline SLOs are defined, alerts are live, and runbook links are present in alert payloads.
- Oncall playbook includes validation queries + safe backfill steps.
- Access controls: feature flag + RBAC enforced; initial allowlist includes Finance + specified Eng/Product roles; access is auditable.

## Open questions
- Do we ship separate “Live” vs “Finance” views in v1, or can we meet freshness expectations with a single cached view (needs SRE + Finance alignment)?
- How do we message “blended” vs “marginal” cost to prevent misreads (Design guidelines + tooltip language)?
- What is the minimum acceptable variance for reconciliation vs billing totals for v1 signoff?

## Risks / watchouts
- Streaming token undercounting causes false cost spikes/drops (mitigation: canary + tests + completeness alerts).
- Tier mapping ambiguity during plan migrations (mitigation: single source of truth + backfill + documented decision rules).
- Warehouse performance under top-N/drilldown queries (mitigation: materializations/partitioning and query caching).
- Data privacy: avoid exposing customer identifiers in top-N/drilldown tables (aggregate rules + redaction).

## Rollout plan
1) Internal dogfood (Eng/Telemetry/Console) → verify parity and query performance
2) Finance dogfood (Rishi + FP&A) → reconciliation + methodology notes + feedback on default views
3) Broader internal (Product/Optimize) → validate drilldowns are sufficient for optimization prioritization
4) Go/no-go checklist: SLOs green, reconciliation within tolerance, RBAC in place

## Notes
- Please route methodology changes (rate card, allocation model, inclusion/exclusion rules) through PM-483 + ADR update so v1 doesn’t drift mid-quarter.
- Any request to add new drilldown dimensions must be reviewed against telemetry cardinality constraints.
